# Design

Two waves. Wave 1 builds three foundations that share no file, so all three proceed in parallel: the runner image with its self-check, the controller with its tests, and the workflow routing with its policy check and canary. Wave 2 deploys both apps once from an operator shell, turns the variable on and proves the canary ran on a Fly runner; it is the only task that touches anything outside the repository.

## The runner image

ubuntu:24.04 pinned by digest, the actions/runner release pinned by version and verified by its published sha256, installed under /home/runner/actions-runner for an unprivileged user runner who has passwordless sudo because eleven workflows install packages with it. The image carries the compilers and system libraries the routed jobs call directly: build-essential, clang, llvm, lld, cmake, ninja, pkg-config, libssl-dev, libclang-dev, git, git-lfs, curl, jq, unzip, zip, xz-utils, zstd, python3 with pip and venv, socat, ca-certificates, gnupg, locales, tzdata, rsync, file, bc and rustup for the runner user with the stable toolchain and the wasm32-unknown-unknown target. Go, Node, Java, Swift, Foundry and Rust versions keep arriving through the setup actions the workflows already use; the tool cache directory /opt/hostedtoolcache exists, is owned by runner and is exported as RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE so those actions cache into it.

entrypoint.sh runs as root, refuses to start without RUNNER_JITCONFIG, drops to the runner user and executes run.sh --jitconfig with that value, watches the runner's output and terminates it when no job has started within RUNNER_IDLE_TIMEOUT seconds (default 900), and exits when the single job ends. It also implements --selfcheck, which prints the runner version, asserts every tool the image promises is on PATH for the runner user and that sudo works without a password, and exits non-zero on the first missing tool. The image's fly.toml declares the app paxeer-ci-runners with no services and no processes, because machines of this app are created only by the controller.

## The controller

Every poll interval the controller lists the repository's workflow runs with status queued and in_progress using conditional requests so unchanged pages cost no rate limit, lists the jobs of each run, and selects jobs whose status is queued and whose requested labels are all within the set self-hosted, linux, x64 and the configured labels, case-insensitively. For every selected job without a live machine carrying its id in machine metadata, while the count of live machines is below the ceiling, it requests a just-in-time configuration from GitHub named fly-<job id> with the configured labels in the default runner group and work folder _work, then creates a machine in the runner app from the configured image with the configuration in RUNNER_JITCONFIG, the configured guest size and region, auto_destroy true, restart policy no, and metadata naming the job id and the run id. A failure of either call is logged with the job id and retried on the next poll; a rate-limit response sleeps until the reset the response names.

Every poll the controller also lists the runner app's machines and destroys any machine whose job is no longer queued or in progress five minutes after the job's completion, any machine older than the orphan ceiling, and any machine in the stopped state that auto_destroy did not remove. Machines without the controller's metadata key are never touched.

Standard library only, a single package main under tools/flyci/controller inside the root module, built with the repository's Go version into a distroless-style image from its own Dockerfile, deployed to the app paxeer-ci-controller as one shared-cpu-1x machine with 512 MB, no public service, and the secrets GITHUB_TOKEN and FLY_API_TOKEN. The Fly token is an app-scoped deploy token for paxeer-ci-runners, never an organization token.

## Routing the jobs

Every routed Linux job's runs-on becomes exactly ${{ (github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name != github.repository) && '<previous>' || vars.CI_LINUX_RUNNER || '<previous>' }} where <previous> is the string the job had before: ubuntu-24.04 or ubuntu-latest. Nothing else in the job changes. .github/actionlint.yaml declares the self-hosted labels layerx-testnet and fly-linux so actionlint knows them.

tools/ci/runner-routing-check.sh loads every workflow with python3 and yaml, and fails naming the file and job when a Linux job outside the explicit exclusion list still has a fixed GitHub-hosted runs-on, when a job inside the exclusion list has anything but its original runs-on, or when an expression differs from the required form. The exclusion list is written in the script as workflow names and job names, one per line, with the reason class beside each.

.github/workflows/runner-canary.yml has one workflow_dispatch job on the routed expression that prints the runner name and labels from the runner environment, compiles and runs a one-line C program with clang and with gcc, prints cargo's and rustup's versions, links with lld, and fails if any of those is missing. Its checkout action is pinned to the same commit the other workflows use.

## Deploying once

From an operator shell already logged in to Fly and GitHub: build the runner image locally, tag it registry.fly.io/paxeer-ci-runners:<commit>, push it after fly auth docker; create the app-scoped deploy token for paxeer-ci-runners; set the controller's secrets GITHUB_TOKEN, FLY_API_TOKEN and RUNNER_IMAGE; deploy the controller from its fly.toml; set the repository variable CI_LINUX_RUNNER to fly-linux; dispatch the canary and read its job back through the API, requiring a runner name that starts with fly- and a successful conclusion. Each step's command, exit code and log path are the task's evidence; nothing in the steps is recorded in a file the repository publishes.
